title: Deep learning enables discovery of highly potent anti-osteoporosis natural products.
summary: A pretrained self-attentive message-passing network prioritized natural products for anti-osteoclastogenesis screening. Five of ten selected virtual hits were confirmed; two were nanomolar inhibitors with new scaffolds and follow-up changes in osteoclast-related gene expression. These are in-vitro findings, not osteoporosis treatment evidence.
organization: Guangdong Academy of Sciences; Sun Yat-sen University; Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports five confirmed hits among ten selected virtual hits from a natural-product library. Two were nanomolar anti-osteoclastogenesis inhibitors with changes in RANK, Ctsk, Nfatc1 and Tracp expression. Biological-replicate counts, protocols and baseline-model metrics were not assessed from the abstract.
evidence.unknown: Full assay protocols, comparator compounds, replicate counts and model-comparison metrics were not reviewed. In-vitro osteoclastogenesis/expression endpoints do not establish clinical osteoporosis benefit; animal-level results were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained self-attentive message-passing neural network, developed on anti-osteoclastogenesis data, ranked natural products for phenotype-based experimental screening.

source_review.scope: Full PubMed primary abstract and metadata; ScienceDirect publisher article identified, but full-text retrieval was blocked and Methods were not reviewed.
